questions.stem: In which direction does conventional current flow in a circuit?

options.text: From negative terminal to positive terminal
From positive terminal to negative terminal
In the same direction as electron flow
Conventional current does not have a direction

questions.explanation: Conventional current flows from the positive terminal to the negative terminal of a battery. This is the opposite direction to actual electron flow, which goes from negative to positive. The convention was established before the discovery of electrons.

questions.stem: Which instrument is used to measure electric current, and how is it connected in a circuit?
questions.explanation: An ammeter is used to measure electric current and must be connected in series with the component being measured. This ensures all the current being measured flows through the ammeter.
